chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Za'lani, from Abu Ismail, raising it from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him),
that he (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Beware of swearing the oath, for it frees up the price and it obliterates the Blessings'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic consequence of using oaths during buying and selling?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns that using oaths in trade, while it may quickly sell the merchandise, ultimately depletes its spiritual value and removes divine blessings (barakah). This teaching highlights the Shia emphasis on sincerity in transactions, contrasting the temporary gain of a sale with the long-term spiritual consequence of diminishing one's share of God's bounty. The phrase 'yufniq al-silah' (consumes the merchandise) is interpreted by scholars as the gradual erosion of the item's intrinsic worth or the buyer's satisfaction due to the lack of truthfulness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Za’laan, from Abu Ismail, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>
that he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Beware of swearing the oath, for it frees up the price and it obliterates the Blessings’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Tsa from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan Za’lan from abu Tsma’il; in a marfu’ manner’ has said, the following: “Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ‘
Beware of swearing; it may make a merchandise easily sell, but it destroys the blessings.’”
